assertions.title: Public booking detail and guest booking detail reuse one booking-detail model

steps.expected: Comparison harness shows public and guest booking-detail fixtures side by side for the same cancelled booking state
steps.observed: Harness rendered both public and guest booking-detail fixtures with matching cancelled status, The Fox venue, REF NB3456, identical guest info, and disabled modify/cancel/book-again actions.

steps.action: Follow the public panel Sign In target
steps.expected: Public panel preserves route-appropriate access by targeting sign-in with recovery flow returning to /bookings/[bookingId]

steps.action: Reopen harness and follow the guest panel Sign In target
steps.expected: Guest panel preserves route-appropriate access by targeting sign-in with recovery flow returning to /guest/bookings/[bookingId]

evidence.consoleErrors: none; console showed expected dev/info logs plus a pre-existing Next.js smooth-scroll warning.
evidence.network: Harness page loaded successfully. Public target final URL encoded next=/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555; guest target final URL encoded next=/guest/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555.

assertions.title: Recovery flow preserves destination continuity end to end

steps.action: Inspect the sign-in targets exposed by the cancelled comparison harness
steps.expected: Recovery flow should target booking recovery and preserve different final destinations for public and guest booking-detail routes without exposing the token after continuation
steps.observed: Harness exposed distinct redirectedFrom values that wrapped /bookings/recover with next=/bookings/... for the public panel and next=/guest/bookings/... for the guest panel.

steps.action: Open a direct recovery URL on the live surface using the harness-shaped path
steps.expected: Recovery should route through recovery and land on the intended internal booking surface while stripping the token from the final URL
steps.observed: Direct navigation to /bookings/recover?access_token=sr1.test-token&next=%2Fbookings%2F55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555 redirected to /bookings/recover/error?code=INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN&reason=invalid_format instead of reaching a final booking-detail destination.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; browser errors stayed empty during the direct recovery attempt.

assertions.issues: Fresh live validation could confirm the distinct public vs guest recovery targets, but not a successful end-to-end recovery continuation because the available direct recovery attempt resolved to the invalid-token error surface instead of a final internal booking route.

frictions.description: agent-browser refs from the initial annotated screenshot could not be reused after a reopen command until a fresh snapshot was taken.
frictions.resolution: Ran agent-browser snapshot -i on the reopened harness and then clicked the refreshed guest-panel Sign In ref.

summary: Tested 2 assertions: 1 passed (VAL-CROSS-003) and 1 failed (VAL-CROSS-004). The comparison harness currently shows shared booking-detail parity plus distinct public/guest sign-in continuity targets, but the live direct recovery attempt ended on the invalid-token error route rather than a token-stripped final booking-detail destination.
